chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When you arrive in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah while you are in the state of Tamattu', you have the time between your arrival and the night to perform Tawaf around the House and Sa'i, and to make that (Tawaf and Sa'i) your Umrah (for Tamattu')."

key_terms.تَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ: To perform Tawaf around the Kaaba
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٌ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Umrah (the ritual act of worship for Tamattu')
key_terms.وَتَسْعَى: And to perform Sa'i (running between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah, the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' upon arriving in Mecca on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal flexibility for a Mutamatti' pilgrim to perform the Umrah rites (Tawaf and Sa'i) upon reaching Mecca on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the Umrah acts serve as the requisite 'mut'ah' (pleasure/exemption) that releases the pilgrim from the strict Ihram constraints of Hajj until the Day of Arafat.
